title: IIT JAM 2027 Chemistry (CY) — Full Length Mock Test 07
titleEn: IIT JAM 2027 Chemistry (CY) — Full Length Mock Test 07

questions.questionTextEn: In an Ellingham diagram (plot of $\Delta_r G^\circ$ per mole of $\text{O}_2$ versus $T$), the line corresponding to the reaction $2\text{C}(s) + \text{O}_2(g) \to 2\text{CO}(g)$ has a
optionsEn: positive slope below $1000\text{ K}$ and zero slope above $1000\text{ K}$
questions.explanationEn: Since $\Delta_r G^\circ = \Delta_r H^\circ - T\Delta_r S^\circ$, the slope of the line is $-\Delta_r S^\circ$. For $2\text{C}(s) + \text{O}_2(g) \to 2\text{CO}(g)$, $\Delta n_g = 2 - 1 = +1 > 0$, so $\Delta_r S^\circ > 0$ and the slope ($-\Delta_r S^\circ$) is negative.

questions.questionTextEn: A reversible Carnot engine operates between a hot reservoir at $600\text{ K}$ and a cold reservoir at $300\text{ K}$. Its thermal efficiency is
questions.explanationEn: The Carnot efficiency is $\eta = 1 - \frac{T_c}{T_h} = 1 - \frac{300}{600} = 0.50$, or $50\%$.

questions.questionTextEn: The basicity (number of ionizable protons in aqueous solution) of hypophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$) and phosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$), respectively, are
questions.explanationEn: Only protons attached to oxygen ($-\text{OH}$) are acidic in phosphorus oxoacids. $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$ has structure $\text{H}_2\text{P}(=\text{O})(\text{OH})$ (one $-\text{OH}$, monobasic, basicity $= 1$), whereas $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$ has structure $\text{HP}(=\text{O})(\text{OH})_2$ (two $-\text{OH}$ groups, dibasic, basicity $= 2$).

questions.questionTextEn: Pyrolysis of 1-phenylethyl acetate ($\text{PhCH(OAc)CH}_3$) at $450\,^\circ\text{C}$ to give styrene and acetic acid proceeds through
questions.explanationEn: Thermal ester pyrolysis proceeds via an **intramolecular *syn*-elimination ($\text{E}_i$)** through a planar six-membered cyclic transition state in which the carbonyl oxygen abstracts a *syn* $\beta$-hydrogen as the $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bond cleaves. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In the Lindemann–Hinshelwood mechanism for unimolecular gas-phase isomerization ($A + A \xrightleftharpoons[k_{-1}]{k_1} A^* + A$, $A^* \xrightarrow{k_2} P$), the effective rate constant $k_{\text{uni}}$ in the high-pressure limit ($k_{-1}[A] \gg k_2$) approaches
questions.explanationEn: Applying the steady-state approximation to $A^*$ yields $k_{\text{uni}} = \frac{k_1 k_2 [A]}{k_{-1}[A] + k_2}$. In the high-pressure limit where $k_{-1}[A] \gg k_2$, $[A]$ cancels and $k_{\text{uni}} \to \frac{k_1 k_2}{k_{-1}}$ (first-order kinetics).

questions.questionTextEn: The Paal–Knorr synthesis of 2,5-dimethylfuran is accomplished by treating hexane-2,5-dione with
questions.explanationEn: In the **Paal–Knorr synthesis**, acid-catalyzed dehydrative cyclization of a 1,4-diketone (hexane-2,5-dione) with $\text{P}_2\text{O}_5$ or $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ yields a **furan** (2,5-dimethylfuran). Using $\text{P}_2\text{S}_5$ gives a thiophene, and using $\text{NH}_3$ gives a pyrrole. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In the neutral-ligand electron-counting method, a **linear** terminal nitrosyl ligand ($\text{M}-\text{N}-\text{O} \approx 180^\circ$) and a **bent** terminal nitrosyl ligand ($\text{M}-\text{N}-\text{O} \approx 120^\circ$) contribute, respectively,
questions.explanationEn: In the neutral-ligand counting scheme, linear $\text{NO}$ (formally $\text{NO}^+$ in the ionic method) donates $3$ electrons, whereas bent $\text{NO}$ (formally $\text{NO}^-$ in the ionic method, with a lone pair on nitrogen) donates $1$ electron.

questions.questionTextEn: For a one-dimensional quantum harmonic oscillator, the vibrational selection rule for electric-dipole transitions is
questions.explanationEn: Under the harmonic oscillator approximation, the transition dipole moment integral $\langle v' | x | v \rangle$ is non-zero only when $\Delta v = \pm 1$.

questions.questionTextEn: In the galvanic cell $\text{Pt}(s)\,|\,\text{H}_2(\text{g}, 1\text{ bar})\,|\,\text{H}^+(\text{aq}, 1\text{ M})\,||\,\text{Ag}^+(\text{aq}, 1\text{ M})\,|\,\text{Ag}(s)$, which species is reduced during spontaneous discharge? [Given: $E^\circ(\text{Ag}^+/\text{Ag}) = +0.80\text{ V}$]
questions.explanationEn: Since $E^\circ(\text{Ag}^+/\text{Ag}) = +0.80\text{ V} > E^\circ(\text{H}^+/\text{H}_2) = 0.00\text{ V}$, the right-hand $\text{Ag}^+/\text{Ag}$ electrode acts as the cathode where $\text{Ag}^+(\text{aq}) + e^- \to \text{Ag}(s)$ reduction occurs spontaneously.

questions.questionTextEn: Among the stereoisomers of dimethylcyclohexane, the isomer whose most stable chair conformation has **zero** 1,3-diaxial $\text{CH}_3\text{–H}$ interactions and **zero** gauche $\text{CH}_3\text{–CH}_3$ interactions is
questions.explanationEn: *trans*-1,4-Dimethylcyclohexane adopts a $(1\text{e},4\text{e})$ diequatorial chair with neither 1,3-diaxial methyl interactions nor any vicinal gauche $\text{CH}_3\text{–CH}_3$ interaction (unlike *trans*-1,2-dimethylcyclohexane, which retains one $\text{CH}_3\text{–CH}_3$ gauche interaction in its diequatorial chair).

questions.questionTextEn: In the crystalline structure of borax, $\text{Na}_2[\text{B}_4\text{O}_5(\text{OH})_4]\cdot 8\text{H}_2\text{O}$, the anionic unit $[\text{B}_4\text{O}_5(\text{OH})_4]^{2-}$ contains
optionsEn: four $sp^3$ boron atoms and zero $sp^2$ boron atoms
two $sp^2$ trigonal planar boron atoms and two $sp^3$ tetrahedral boron atoms
three $sp^2$ boron atoms and one $sp^3$ boron atom
questions.explanationEn: The $[\text{B}_4\text{O}_5(\text{OH})_4]^{2-}$ anion consists of two fused six-membered $\text{B}_3\text{O}_3$ rings sharing a central $\text{B}-\text{O}-\text{B}$ bridge. The two boron atoms linked by the central oxygen bridge are $4$-coordinate ($sp^3$, tetrahedral), while the other two boron atoms are $3$-coordinate ($sp^2$, trigonal planar). Each boron bears one terminal $-\text{OH}$ group.

questions.questionTextEn: The temperature at which the root-mean-square speed of $\text{O}_2$ ($M = 32\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) equals the root-mean-square speed of $\text{H}_2$ ($M = 2\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) at $300\text{ K}$ is
questions.explanationEn: Equating $v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}$ for both gases gives $\frac{T_{\text{O}_2}}{M_{\text{O}_2}} = \frac{T_{\text{H}_2}}{M_{\text{H}_2}} \implies T_{\text{O}_2} = 300 \times \frac{32}{2} = 4800\text{ K}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The correct decreasing order of acidity in water for phenol (**I**), *o*-nitrophenol (**II**), *m*-nitrophenol (**III**), and *p*-nitrophenol (**IV**) is
questions.explanationEn: Both *p*-nitrophenol ($\text{p}K_a = 7.15$) and *o*-nitrophenol ($\text{p}K_a = 7.23$) stabilize the phenoxide ion by both $-M$ and $-I$ effects, but intramolecular H-bonding in *o*-nitrophenol slightly stabilizes the neutral acid, making **IV** slightly more acidic than **II**. *m*-Nitrophenol ($\text{p}K_a = 8.36$) benefits only from $-I$, and unsubstituted phenol ($\text{p}K_a = 9.95$) is the weakest.

questions.questionTextEn: An aromatic compound $\text{C}_8\text{H}_8\text{O}$ gives a yellow precipitate with $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$, a negative Tollens' test, a strong IR band at $1685\text{ cm}^{-1}$, and a $3\text{H}$ singlet at $\delta\ 2.60\text{ ppm}$ in its $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrum. The compound is
questions.explanationEn: A positive iodoform test, negative Tollens' test, conjugated aryl ketone IR stretch at $1685\text{ cm}^{-1}$, and a $3\text{H}$ singlet at $\delta\ 2.60\text{ ppm}$ ($-\text{COCH}_3$) uniquely identify **acetophenone**.

questions.questionTextEn: Reaction of cyclohex-2-en-1-one with $\text{Me}_2\text{CuLi}$ followed by trapping the intermediate enolate with $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ (instead of aqueous protonation) yields predominantly
questions.explanationEn: $\text{Me}_2\text{CuLi}$ performs 1,4-conjugate addition to cyclohex-2-en-1-one, placing a methyl group at C3 and generating a lithium enolate across $\text{C1}=\text{C2}$. Subsequent alkylation with $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ approaches C2 from the less sterically hindered face **anti (*trans*)** to the C3 methyl group, yielding ***trans*-2,3-dimethylcyclohexan-1-one**. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: When monochromatic radiation of photon energy $5.0\text{ eV}$ strikes a metallic cathode, the stopping potential required to halt the emitted photoelectrons is $3.0\text{ V}$. If the incident photon energy is increased to $7.5\text{ eV}$, the new stopping potential will be
questions.explanationEn: By Einstein's photoelectric equation, $eV_s = h\nu - \phi$. From the first experiment, $\phi = 5.0\text{ eV} - 3.0\text{ eV} = 2.0\text{ eV}$. At $h\nu' = 7.5\text{ eV}$, $eV_s' = 7.5 - 2.0 = 5.5\text{ eV}$, giving a stopping potential of $5.5\text{ V}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The yellow-brown nitro complex $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5(\text{NO}_2)]\text{Cl}_2$ ($N$-bound) and the red nitrito complex $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5(\text{ONO})]\text{Cl}_2$ ($O$-bound) are linkage isomers. How are they most readily distinguished by infrared spectroscopy?
optionsEn:
The $O$-bound nitrito isomer shows a much larger separation between $
u_{	ext{asym}}(	ext{NO}_2)$ and $
u_{	ext{sym}}(	ext{NO}_2)$ (with $
u_{	ext{asym}} \approx 1470	ext{ cm}^{-1}$, $
u_{	ext{sym}} \approx 1065	ext{ cm}^{-1}$) than the $N$-bound nitro isomer ($1430	ext{ cm}^{-1}$ and $1310	ext{ cm}^{-1}$).
The $N$-bound nitro isomer is IR-inactive in the $1000\text{--}1500\text{ cm}^{-1}$ region.
Only the $N$-bound isomer exhibits $\text{N}-\text{H}$ stretching bands.
The $O$-bound isomer has identical $\text{N}-\text{O}$ bond lengths and therefore shows only one $\text{N}-\text{O}$ stretching band.
questions.explanationEn: In the $O$-bound nitrito isomer ($\text{Co}-\text{O}-\text{N}=\text{O}$), one $\text{N}-\text{O}$ bond has single-bond character and the other has double-bond character, producing a wide split between $\nu(\text{N}=\text{O}) \approx 1470\text{ cm}^{-1}$ and $\nu(\text{N}-\text{O}) \approx 1065\text{ cm}^{-1}$. In the symmetric $N$-bound nitro isomer, both $\text{N}-\text{O}$ bonds are equivalent, giving closer bands at $\sim 1430$ and $1310\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn:
The thermal decomposition of ozone ($2\text{O}_3 \to 3\text{O}_2$) proceeds by the mechanism:
Step 1: $\text{O}_3 \xrightleftharpoons[k_{-1}]{k_1} \text{O}_2 + \text{O}$
Step 2: $\text{O} + \text{O}_3 \xrightarrow{k_2} 2\text{O}_2$
Applying the steady-state approximation to $\text{O}$, the rate of disappearance of $\text{O}_3$, $-\frac{d[\text{O}_3]}{dt}$, is
questions.explanationEn: Steady state for $\text{O}$: $k_1[\text{O}_3] - k_{-1}[\text{O}_2][\text{O}] - k_2[\text{O}][\text{O}_3] = 0 \implies [\text{O}] = \frac{k_1[\text{O}_3]}{k_{-1}[\text{O}_2] + k_2[\text{O}_3]}$. Then $-\frac{d[\text{O}_3]}{dt} = k_1[\text{O}_3] - k_{-1}[\text{O}_2][\text{O}] + k_2[\text{O}][\text{O}_3] = 2k_2[\text{O}][\text{O}_3] = \frac{2k_1 k_2[\text{O}_3]^2}{k_{-1}[\text{O}_2] + k_2[\text{O}_3]}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Menthol (2-isopropyl-5-methylcyclohexan-1-ol), a cyclic monoterpene alcohol, adopts a most stable chair conformation in which its three substituents ($-\text{CH}_3$, $-\text{OH}$, and $-\text{CH(CH}_3)_2$) are arranged as
questions.explanationEn: Naturally occurring $(-)$-menthol is $(1R,2S,5R)$-2-isopropyl-5-methylcyclohexan-1-ol, which is uniquely the stereoisomer where **all three substituents ($\text{C1}-\text{OH}$, $\text{C2}-i\text{-Pr}$, and $\text{C5}-\text{Me}$) occupy equatorial positions simultaneously** in the chair conformation, explaining its exceptional conformational stability. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Intramolecular aldol condensation of hexane-2,5-dione upon heating with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ yields predominantly
questions.explanationEn: Hexane-2,5-dione can form an enolate at C1 (terminal methyl) or C3 (internal methylene). Attack of the C3 enolate on C5 would produce a strained 3-membered ring (disfavored). Attack of the C1 enolate on the C5 ketone forms a thermodynamically favored 5-membered ring, which dehydrates on heating to **3-methylcyclopent-2-en-1-one**. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In gravimetric analysis (such as precipitating $\text{BaSO}_4$), the freshly formed precipitate is heated gently in contact with its mother liquor (**digestion**) before filtration primarily to
optionsEn: increase the relative supersaturation so smaller colloidal particles form
promote dissolution of fine particles and regrowth onto larger crystals (Ostwald ripening), improving filterability and reducing coprecipitated surface impurities
convert crystalline precipitates into gelatinous colloids
questions.explanationEn: Digestion allows smaller, higher-surface-energy microcrystals to dissolve and reprecipitate onto larger crystals (Ostwald ripening), yielding larger, purer, easily filterable crystals with reduced adsorbed impurities.

questions.questionTextEn: For a buffer solution prepared from a weak monoprotic acid $\text{HA}$ and its conjugate base $\text{A}^-$ at fixed total concentration $C_{\text{total}} = [\text{HA}] + [\text{A}^-]$, the buffer capacity is **maximum** when
questions.explanationEn: The buffer capacity $\beta = 2.303\frac{C_{\text{total}} K_a [\text{H}^+]}{(K_a + [\text{H}^+])^2}$ is maximized when $[\text{H}^+] = K_a$, i.e., when $[\text{HA}] = [\text{A}^-]$ and $\text{pH} = \text{p}K_a$.

questions.questionTextEn: In the $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrum of $[18]$-annulene at $-60\ ^\circ\text{C}$, the $12$ outer protons resonate near $\delta\ 9.3\text{ ppm}$ whereas the $6$ inner protons resonate near $\delta\ -3.0\text{ ppm}$. This dramatic shielding of the inner protons is direct evidence of
optionsEn: a paratropic ring current characteristic of an antiaromatic $4n\pi$ system.
strong intramolecular hydrogen bonding among the six inner protons.
rapid valence tautomerization into localized single and double bonds.
a diatropic ring current characteristic of an aromatic $(4n+2)\pi$ system ($n = 4$).
questions.explanationEn: $[18]$-Annulene is planar and has $18\pi$ electrons ($4n + 2$ with $n = 4$), sustaining an aromatic **diatropic** ring current that reinforces the applied magnetic field outside the ring (deshielding outer protons to $\delta\ 9.3$) and opposes it inside the ring (strongly shielding inner protons to $\delta\ -3.0$).

questions.questionTextEn: Acid-catalyzed hydration/cyclization of **geraniol** or **nerol** yields $\alpha$-terpineol. Why does **nerol** (the $(Z)$-isomer) cyclize dramatically faster than **geraniol** (the $(E)$-isomer) to form $\alpha$-terpineol?
optionsEn: Nerol forms a more stable primary carbocation

In nerol, the $(Z)$-$\text{C2}=\text{C3}$ double bond places the $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ group *cis* to the alkenyl chain, pre-organizing the allylic cation for direct 6-membered ring closure without $E/Z$ isomerization
Geraniol cannot be protonated by aqueous acid
Nerol undergoes a concerted Diels–Alder cycloaddition
questions.explanationEn: Upon protonation and loss of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ from **nerol**, the resulting $(Z)$-allylic carbocation already has the C1 carbon positioned *cis* to the $\text{C6}=\text{C7}$ double bond, enabling immediate intramolecular electrophilic cyclization to the 6-membered $\alpha$-terpinyl cation. In **geraniol** ($(E)$-isomer), C1 is *trans* to the $\text{C6}=\text{C7}$ chain and cannot directly close the ring without prior isomerization. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: During the Hall–Héroult electrolytic extraction of aluminium from molten $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ dissolved in cryolite using graphite electrodes, the graphite anodes must be periodically replaced because
optionsEn: molten aluminium dissolves graphite at the anode
oxygen liberated at the anode reacts with the hot graphite to form $\text{CO}$ and $\text{CO}_2$
questions.explanationEn: At the graphite anodes ($\sim 950\,^\circ\text{C}$), oxide ions discharge and oxidize the carbon anode directly to $\text{CO}$ and $\text{CO}_2$ ($\text{C} + 2\text{O}^{2-} \to \text{CO}_2 + 4e^-$), consuming roughly $0.5\text{ kg}$ of carbon per $\text{kg}$ of $\text{Al}$ produced.

questions.questionTextEn: For the gas-phase dissociation $\text{PCl}_5(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{PCl}_3(g) + \text{Cl}_2(g)$ at equilibrium, adding an inert gas (argon) at **constant temperature and constant total pressure**
optionsEn: shifts the equilibrium toward the products ($\text{PCl}_3$ and $\text{Cl}_2$)
shifts the equilibrium toward the reactant ($\text{PCl}_5$)
questions.explanationEn: Adding an inert gas at constant $T$ and constant total $P$ increases the total volume, lowering the partial pressures of all reacting gases. Because $\Delta n_g = +1 > 0$, the equilibrium shifts toward the side with more moles of gas (products), while $K_p$ remains unchanged at constant $T$.

questions.questionTextEn: In the $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrum of chloroethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$), the methylene ($-\text{CH}_2-$) protons appear as a
questions.explanationEn: The $-\text{CH}_2-$ protons are coupled to $n = 3$ equivalent vicinal $-\text{CH}_3$ protons. By the $(n + 1)$ rule and Pascal's triangle, they split into a quartet ($3 + 1 = 4$ lines) with relative intensities $1:3:3:1$.

questions.questionTextEn: The specific conductivity of a saturated aqueous solution of $\text{AgCl}$ at $298\text{ K}$ is $2.40 \times 10^{-6}\text{ S cm}^{-1}$, while that of the pure water used is $0.60 \times 10^{-6}\text{ S cm}^{-1}$. Given $\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{AgCl}) = 138.3\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$, the solubility product $K_{sp}$ of $\text{AgCl}$ at $298\text{ K}$ is closest to
questions.explanationEn: $\kappa(\text{AgCl}) = (2.40 - 0.60) \times 10^{-6} = 1.80 \times 10^{-6}\text{ S cm}^{-1}$. Molar solubility $s = \frac{1000\,\kappa(\text{AgCl})}{\Lambda_m^\circ} = \frac{1.80 \times 10^{-3}}{138.3} = 1.302e-05\text{ M}$. Thus $K_{sp} = s^2 = 1.69e-10 \approx 1.7 \times 10^{-10}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The intense orange-red color ($\lambda_{\max} \approx 452\text{ nm}$, $\varepsilon \approx 14{,}600\text{ L mol}^{-1}\text{ cm}^{-1}$) of $[\text{Ru(bpy)}_3]^{2+}$ (where $\text{bpy} = 2,2'\text{-bipyridine}$) is attributed to
optionsEn: a metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) transition from filled $\text{Ru}(t_{2g})$ orbitals to empty $\pi^*$ orbitals of $\text{bpy}$
an intervalence charge transfer between $\text{Ru(II)}$ and $\text{Ru(III)}$
questions.explanationEn: $[\text{Ru(bpy)}_3]^{2+}$ has an electron-rich low-spin $4d^6$ $\text{Ru(II)}$ center coordinated to conjugated $\pi$-acceptor $2,2'$-bipyridine ligands possessing low-lying empty $\pi^*$ orbitals, producing a classic intense MLCT ($d\pi \to \pi^*$) absorption.

questions.questionTextEn: Treatment of methyl $\alpha$-D-glucopyranoside with excess $\text{NaIO}_4$ cleaves the pyranose ring, consuming $2\text{ moles}$ of $\text{NaIO}_4$ per mole of glycoside and liberating $1\text{ mole}$ of which small organic byproduct?
questions.explanationEn: In methyl $\alpha$-D-glucopyranoside, C2, C3, and C4 bear three contiguous free $-\text{OH}$ groups. Periodic acid cleaves both the $\text{C2}-\text{C3}$ and $\text{C3}-\text{C4}$ bonds (consuming $2\text{ mol NaIO}_4$). The central **C3** ($-\text{CH(OH)}-$) is flanked by two cleaved bonds and is oxidized completely to **$1\text{ mol}$ of formic acid ($\text{HCO}_2\text{H}$)**, while C2 and C4 become aldehyde groups in the dialdehyde fragment. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: For a zero-order reaction $A \to P$ with rate constant $k$ and initial concentration $[A]_0$, the correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: The rate of reaction is constant and equal to $k$ until $A$ is completely consumed.
The half-life $t_{1/2}$ is directly proportional to $[A]_0$.
The reaction reaches $100\%$ completion in finite time $t_{\text{comp}} = [A]_0/k$.
questions.explanationEn: For zero-order kinetics, $[A]_t = [A]_0 - kt$, rate $= k$ (units $\text{mol dm}^{-3}\text{ s}^{-1}$, so D is false), $t_{1/2} = [A]_0/(2k) \propto [A]_0$, and completion occurs at $t = [A]_0/k$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following dienes react readily as the $4\pi$ component in a normal-electron-demand Diels–Alder reaction with tetracyanoethylene (TCNE)?
questions.explanationEn:
A diene must easily adopt the ***s-cis*** conformation to undergo Diels–Alder cycloaddition:
- **(A) Cyclopenta-1,3-diene:** Rigidly locked *s-cis* $\implies$ reacts extremely fast.
- **(B) 1,2-Dimethylenecyclohexane:** Easily adopts *s-cis* with no internal steric clash $\implies$ reacts readily.
- **(C) $(2Z,4Z)$-Hexa-2,4-diene:** Severe steric clash between the two internal *Z*-methyl groups prevents it from adopting the planar *s-cis* conformation $\implies$ essentially unreactive.
- **(D) Cyclohexa-1,3-diene:** Locked *s-cis* $\implies$ reacts readily.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (D)** are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about diborane ($\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$) is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: The bridging $\text{B}-\text{H}$ bond length is longer than the terminal $\text{B}-\text{H}$ bond length.
All six hydrogen atoms and both boron atoms lie in the same molecular plane.
Diborane reacts with water to produce boric acid ($\text{H}_3\text{BO}_3$) and $\text{H}_2$ gas.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A) True: Each boron forms two terminal $2\text{c}\text{--}2\text{e}$ bonds and two bridging $3\text{c}\text{--}2\text{e}$ bonds using four $sp^3$ hybrid orbitals.
- (B) True: Bridging $\text{B}-\text{H}$ ($131\text{ pm}$, bond order $\approx 0.5$) is longer than terminal $\text{B}-\text{H}$ ($119\text{ pm}$, bond order $1$).
- (C) False: Only the two $\text{B}$ atoms and four terminal $\text{H}$ atoms are coplanar; the two bridging $\text{H}$ atoms lie above and below that plane.
- (D) True: $\text{B}_2\text{H}_6 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \to 2\text{H}_3\text{BO}_3 + 6\text{H}_2$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) regarding silicates and aluminosilicates is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: In quartz ($\text{SiO}_2$), all four oxygen corners of every $\text{SiO}_4$ tetrahedron are shared, forming a neutral 3D framework.

Substitution of some $\text{Si}^{4+}$ ions by $\text{Al}^{3+}$ in a 3D silicate framework creates a negative charge that is balanced by extra-framework cations (e.g., $\text{Na}^+, \text{Ca}^{2+}$) in zeolites and feldspars.
Beryl ($\text{Be}_3\text{Al}_2\text{Si}_6\text{O}_{18}$) is a cyclic silicate containing the $[\text{Si}_6\text{O}_{18}]^{12-}$ ring.
Orthosilicates (nesosilicates) such as zircon ($\text{ZrSiO}_4$) contain $\text{Si}-\text{O}-\text{Si}$ bridges.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A) True: Quartz is a 3D tectosilicate with $4$ shared corners per $\text{SiO}_4$.
- (B) True: Replacing $\text{Si}^{4+}$ with $\text{Al}^{3+}$ introduces a $-1$ charge per substitution, balanced by $\text{Na}^+, \text{K}^+, \text{Ca}^{2+}$ ions.
- (C) True: Beryl contains 6-membered cyclic $[\text{Si}_6\text{O}_{18}]^{12-}$ rings.
- (D) False: Orthosilicates contain discrete, isolated $[\text{SiO}_4]^{4-}$ tetrahedra with no $\text{Si}-\text{O}-\text{Si}$ bridges.

questions.questionTextEn: In UV–visible electronic spectroscopy of molecules, the correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: According to the Franck–Condon principle, electronic transitions occur vertically on a potential energy diagram because nuclei move much more slowly than electrons.
Extending conjugated $\pi$-systems shifts the $\pi \to \pi^*$ absorption maximum ($\lambda_{\max}$) to longer wavelengths.
The $n \to \pi^*$ transition in saturated ketones typically has a much larger molar absorptivity ($\varepsilon$) than the $\pi \to \pi^*$ transition.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A), (B), (C) True:** Vertical transitions (Franck–Condon), $\Delta S = 0$ (spin selection rule), and smaller HOMO–LUMO gap with conjugation (longer $\lambda_{\max}$).
- **(D) False:** $n \to \pi^*$ transitions are symmetry-forbidden ($\varepsilon \sim 10\text{--}100$), much weaker than allowed $\pi \to \pi^*$ transitions ($\varepsilon \sim 10^4$).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following substituted cyclohexanes is/are **optically inactive** (achiral or rapidly interconverting conformational racemate) at room temperature?
questions.explanationEn: *cis*-1,4-, *trans*-1,4-, and *cis*-1,3-dimethylcyclohexane all possess planes of symmetry and are achiral. Enantiopure $(1R,2R)$-1,2-dimethylcyclohexane is chiral and optically active (its ring flip gives the $(a,a)$ conformer of the same $(1R,2R)$ enantiomer).

questions.questionTextEn: For a sparingly soluble salt $\text{MX}_2(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{M}^{2+}(aq) + 2\text{X}^-(aq)$ with solubility product $K_{sp}$ and ionic product $Q_{sp} = [\text{M}^{2+}][\text{X}^-]^2$, the correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: Precipitation of $\text{MX}_2(s)$ occurs spontaneously when $Q_{sp} > K_{sp}$.
In pure water, the molar solubility is $s = (K_{sp}/4)^{1/3}$.
Adding a soluble salt containing $\text{X}^-$ decreases the molar solubility of $\text{MX}_2$.
Increasing the amount of excess solid $\text{MX}_2(s)$ in contact with a saturated solution increases $[\text{M}^{2+}]$.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) True:** Supersaturation ($Q_{sp} > K_{sp}$) drives precipitation.
- **(B) True:** $K_{sp} = s(2s)^2 = 4s^3 \implies s = (K_{sp}/4)^{1/3}$.
- **(C) True:** Common-ion effect suppresses dissolution.
- **(D) False:** Pure solid has unit activity; adding more solid does not alter the equilibrium concentration.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following compound(s) give(s) a **positive** 2,4-DNP test AND a **positive** iodoform test?
questions.explanationEn: Acetaldehyde, acetophenone, and butan-2-one are all carbonyl compounds (positive 2,4-DNP) containing a $\text{CH}_3\text{C(=O)}-$ unit (positive iodoform). Propan-2-ol gives a positive iodoform test but a negative 2,4-DNP test.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about the magnetic properties of first-row transition metal complexes is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: The spin-only magnetic moment formula $\mu_s = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\,\mu_B$ agrees closely with experiment for octahedral $d^3$ ($\text{Cr}^{3+}$), high-spin $d^5$ ($\text{Mn}^{2+}$), and $d^8$ ($\text{Ni}^{2+}$) complexes.

Octahedral $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$ (high-spin $d^6$, $^5T_{2g}$) has an observed $\mu_{\text{eff}}$ ($\sim 5.1\text{--}5.5\,\mu_B$) larger than its spin-only value ($4.90\,\mu_B$) due to orbital contribution.
Tetrahedral $[\text{CoCl}_4]^{2-}$ ($d^7$, $^4A_2$) has a smaller orbital contribution than octahedral $[\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$ ($d^7$, $^4T_{1g}$).
questions.explanationEn:
- (A) True: $A$ ground terms ($^4A_{2g}, ^6A_{1g}, ^3A_{2g}$) have quenched first-order orbital angular momentum.
- (B) True: $^5T_{2g}$ ground term retains first-order orbital angular momentum.
- (C) True: $^4A_2$ has no first-order orbital contribution (only second-order spin–orbit mixing), whereas $^4T_{1g}$ has a large first-order orbital contribution.
- (D) False: Low-spin $d^6$ $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ ($t_{2g}^6$) has $0$ unpaired electrons and is diamagnetic.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about **D-glucose** and **D-fructose** is/are correct?
optionsEn: Both D-glucose and D-fructose give a positive Tollens' test (silver mirror).
D-Glucose and D-fructose form the exact same crystalline osazone upon reaction with excess phenylhydrazine.
Both D-glucose and D-fructose are oxidized to D-gluconic acid by mild bromine water ($\text{Br}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}$).
Reduction of D-fructose with $\text{NaBH}_4$ yields a mixture of two C2-epimeric alditols: D-glucitol (sorbitol) and D-mannitol.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** In alkaline Tollens' reagent, D-fructose isomerizes via an enediol to D-glucose and D-mannose, so both give a positive silver-mirror test.
- **(B) Correct:** Both share identical configurations at C3, C4, and C5, giving the same glucosazone.
- **(C) Incorrect:** Mild acidic bromine water oxidizes aldoses (D-glucose $\to$ D-gluconic acid) but does **NOT** oxidize ketoses like D-fructose.
- **(D) Correct:** Reduction of the C2 ketone of D-fructose creates a new stereocenter at C2, producing both D-glucitol and D-mannitol.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (D)** are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: If $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{pmatrix}$, the trace of $A^2$ is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Computing $A^2 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 7 & 10 \\ 15 & 22 \end{pmatrix}$. Its trace is $7 + 22 = 29$.

questions.questionTextEn: The percentage ($\%$) of a radioactive isotope remaining undecayed after $4$ half-lives is _______ $\%$. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: After $n = 4$ half-lives, the remaining fraction is $(1/2)^4 = 1/16 = 0.0625$, which equals $6.25\%$.

questions.questionTextEn: According to the isoprene rule, the number of isoprene ($\text{C}_5$) units that constitute the carbon skeleton of $\beta$-carotene ($\text{C}_{40}\text{H}_{56}$) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: $\beta$-Carotene is a **tetraterpene** containing $40$ carbon atoms, corresponding to $40 / 5 = \mathbf{8}$ isoprene units.

questions.questionTextEn: In the $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrum of 2-bromopropane ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHBr}$), the number of lines in the multiplet due to the methine ($-\text{CHBr}-$) proton is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: The methine proton is coupled equally to $6$ equivalent methyl protons, so by the $(n + 1)$ rule it splits into $6 + 1 = 7$ lines (a septet).

questions.questionTextEn: The total number of stereoisomers formed when $(E)$-hex-3-ene is treated with catalytic $\text{OsO}_4$ and NMO is _______.
questions.explanationEn: *Syn*-dihydroxylation of $(E)$-hex-3-ene yields exclusively the racemic pair $(3R,4R)$-hexane-3,4-diol and $(3S,4S)$-hexane-3,4-diol. Thus, **$2$** stereoisomers are formed.

questions.questionTextEn: The number of lone pairs of electrons on the central iodine atom in the triiodide ion $\text{I}_3^-$ is _______.
questions.explanationEn: The central iodine atom has $7$ valence electrons plus $1$ for the negative charge ($8$ total). Two $\text{I}-\text{I}$ bonds use $2$ electrons, leaving $6$ non-bonding electrons, i.e., $3$ lone pairs occupying the equatorial sites of a trigonal bipyramid.

questions.questionTextEn: The total ionic strength of an aqueous solution that is $0.10\text{ M}$ in $\text{NaCl}$ and $0.05\text{ M}$ in $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4$ is _______ $\text{M}$. *(round off to two decimal places)*

Adsorption of a gas on charcoal follows the Freundlich isotherm $x/m = k P^{1/n}$ with $k = 0.40\text{ g g}^{-1}\text{ bar}^{-1/2}$ and $n = 2$. The mass of gas adsorbed by $5.0\text{ g}$ of charcoal at $P = 9.0\text{ bar}$ is _______ $\text{g}$. *(round off to one decimal place)*
The number of lone pairs of electrons on the central xenon atom in the pentagonal planar anion $[\text{XeF}_5]^-$ is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Xenon contributes $8$ valence electrons, the $-1$ charge adds $1$ electron, and $5$ $\text{Xe}-\text{F}$ single bonds use $5$ electrons, leaving $8 + 1 - 5 = 4$ non-bonding electrons, i.e., $2$ lone pairs (axial positions in a pentagonal bipyramidal electron arrangement).

questions.questionTextEn: When $0.10\text{ mol}$ of a non-volatile, non-electrolyte solute is dissolved in $0.90\text{ mol}$ of a pure liquid solvent obeying Raoult's law, the relative lowering of vapor pressure $\dfrac{P^\circ - P}{P^\circ}$ is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: By Raoult's law, $\frac{P^\circ - P}{P^\circ} = x_{\text{solute}} = \frac{0.10}{0.10 + 0.90} = 0.10$.

questions.questionTextEn: Using Slater's rules to evaluate $Z_{\text{eff}}$ for a $3p$ valence electron of silicon ($Z = 14$) and its covalent radius $r_{\text{cov}} = 1.17\text{ \AA}$, calculate the Allred–Rochow electronegativity ($\chi_{\text{AR}} = \dfrac{0.359\,Z_{\text{eff}}}{r_{\text{cov}}^2} + 0.744$) of silicon: _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*

A reactant $A$ undergoes two parallel first-order reactions with Arrhenius parameters $A_1 = 1.0 \times 10^{11}\text{ s}^{-1}$, $E_{a1} = 60.0\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $A_2 = 1.0 \times 10^{13}\text{ s}^{-1}$, $E_{a2} = 80.0\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. Taking $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, the temperature at which the two pathways have equal rate constants ($k_1 = k_2$) is _______ $\text{K}$. *(round off to one decimal place)*
questions.explanationEn: Setting $A_1 e^{-E_{a1}/RT} = A_2 e^{-E_{a2}/RT}$ yields $\ln(A_2/A_1) = \frac{E_{a2} - E_{a1}}{RT} \implies T = \frac{20000}{8.314 \times \ln 100} = 522.37\text{ K} \approx 522.4\text{ K}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The number of chemically non-equivalent sets of protons (signals) in the $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrum of 1,2,3-trimethylbenzene is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: 1,2,3-Trimethylbenzene has a plane of symmetry passing through C2 and C5, giving $4$ proton sets: (1) C2-$\text{CH}_3$ ($3\text{H}$), (2) C1/C3-$\text{CH}_3$ ($6\text{H}$), (3) H4/H6 ($2\text{H}$), and (4) H5 ($1\text{H}$).

questions.questionTextEn:
A monochromatic laser operating at wavelength $662.6\text{ nm}$ emits power at a steady rate of $10\text{ mW}$. The number of photons emitted per second is $X \times 10^{16}$. The value of $X$ is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
[Given: $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}$, $c = 3.0 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}$]
questions.explanationEn: The energy of one photon is $E = \frac{hc}{\lambda} = \frac{6.626\times 10^{-34} \times 3.0\times 10^8}{662.6\times 10^{-9}} = 3.0 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}$. The photon emission rate is $\frac{P}{E} = \frac{10 \times 10^{-3}\text{ J s}^{-1}}{3.0 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}} = 3.33 \times 10^{16}\text{ s}^{-1}$, so $X = 3.33$.

questions.questionTextEn:
Assuming hard-sphere behavior with collision diameter $d = 0.37\text{ nm}$, the mean free path of $\text{N}_2$ gas at $T = 300\text{ K}$ and $P = 1.00\text{ bar}$ ($1.00 \times 10^5\text{ Pa}$) is _______ $\text{nm}$. *(round off to one decimal place)*
[Given: $k_B = 1.3806 \times 10^{-23}\text{ J K}^{-1}$]
questions.explanationEn: Using $\lambda = \frac{k_B T}{\sqrt{2}\pi d^2 P} = \frac{1.3806 \times 10^{-23} \times 300}{\sqrt{2}\pi (3.7 \times 10^{-10})^2 (1.00 \times 10^5)} = 6.81 \times 10^{-8}\text{ m} = 68.1\text{ nm}$.

questions.questionTextEn:
Claisen condensation of $17.6\text{ g}$ of ethyl acetate ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$) with $\text{NaOEt}$ followed by acidic workup affords ethyl acetoacetate ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_3$) in $70\%$ isolated yield. The mass of ethyl acetoacetate obtained is _______ $\text{g}$. *(round off to one decimal place)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{O} = 16$]
questions.explanationEn:
Stoichiometry: $2\,\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{Et} \to \text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{Et} + \text{EtOH}$.
- Moles of ethyl acetate $= 17.6 / 88 = 0.200\text{ mol}$.
- Theoretical moles of ethyl acetoacetate $= 0.100\text{ mol}$, theoretical mass $= 0.100 \times 130 = 13.0\text{ g}$.
- At $70\%$ yield, mass obtained $= 13.0 \times 0.70 = \mathbf{9.1}\text{ g}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The medical radioisotope $^{131}\text{I}$ has a half-life of $8.02\text{ days}$. The time required for $90\%$ of an initial sample of $^{131}\text{I}$ to decay is _______ $\text{days}$. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn:
When $90\%$ has decayed, $10\%$ remains ($N/N_0 = 0.10$).
Using first-order decay kinetics, $t = \frac{t_{1/2}}{\ln 2}\ln\left(\frac{N_0}{N}\right) = \frac{8.02}{0.69315}\ln(10) = 11.5704 \times 2.30259 = 26.64\text{ days}$.

questions.questionTextEn:
In a Hall–Héroult electrolytic cell, a steady current of $10{,}000\text{ A}$ is passed for $2.0\text{ hours}$ at $90\%$ current efficiency. The mass of aluminium deposited at the cathode is _______ $\text{kg}$. *(round off to two decimal places)*

[Given: Atomic mass of $\text{Al} = 27.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}$; Faraday constant $F = 96{,}500\text{ C mol}^{-1}$]
questions.explanationEn:
Effective charge passed: $Q_{\text{eff}} = I \cdot t \cdot \eta = 10{,}000 \times (2.0 \times 3600) \times 0.90 = 6.48 \times 10^7\text{ C}$.
For $\text{Al}^{3+} + 3e^- \to \text{Al}$, moles of $\text{Al} = \frac{6.48 \times 10^7}{3 \times 96{,}500} = 223.834\text{ mol}$.
Mass of $\text{Al} = 223.834 \times 27.0\text{ g} = 6043.5\text{ g} = 6.04\text{ kg}$.

questions.questionTextEn:
Aniline ($9.30\text{ g}$, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_7\text{N}$) is diazotized with $\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}$ at $0\,^\circ\text{C}$ and treated with $\text{CuCN/KCN}$ (Sandmeyer reaction) to yield $7.725\text{ g}$ of benzonitrile ($\text{C}_7\text{H}_5\text{N}$). The overall percentage yield of benzonitrile is _______ $\%$. *(round off to the nearest integer)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{N} = 14$]
questions.explanationEn:
Moles of aniline ($\text{MW} = 93\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) $= 9.30 / 93 = 0.100\text{ mol}$.
Theoretical mass of benzonitrile ($\text{MW} = 103\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) $= 0.100 \times 103 = 10.30\text{ g}$.
Percentage yield $= (7.725 / 10.30) \times 100\% = \mathbf{75}\%$.

questions.questionTextEn: The total number of stereoisomers (including enantiomers) possible for 1,2,3-trimethylcyclohexane is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Classifying by up ($u$) and down ($d$) orientations on C1, C2, C3: (1) $(u,u,u)$ — achiral (*meso*, plane through C2–C5); (2) $(u,d,u)$ — achiral (*meso*, plane through C2–C5); (3) $(u,u,d)$ and its non-superimposable mirror image $(d,d,u)$ — a chiral enantiomeric pair ($2$ isomers). Total $= 1 + 1 + 2 = 4$ stereoisomers.
